title: Taming the tannin
subtitle: How winemakers soften Tannat
objectives: Describe other ways to soften Tannat

steps.title: Born in Madiran
steps.body: In 1991, Madiran winemaker Patrick Ducournau developed micro-oxygenation: tiny, controlled doses of oxygen bubbled into the wine. It helps tannins link into longer chains, which feel softer, and stabilises colour. Born to tame Tannat, the technique is now used all over the world.

steps.title: Other tools
steps.body: Winemakers also soften Tannat by picking when skins and seeds are fully ripe, by gentle extraction, avoiding crushed seeds, by shorter maceration and by ageing in oak, where slow oxygen through the wood helps. In Uruguay, some producers make lighter, fresher Tannat with little oak to drink young.

steps.prompt: What does micro-oxygenation do to Tannat?
options: Helps tannins soften and stabilises colour
steps.explanation: Small, controlled doses of oxygen help tannins polymerise, so they feel softer, and fix colour.

steps.title: Blending
steps.body: Blending is the oldest solution. In Madiran, Cabernet Franc adds perfume and lightness. In Uruguay, Tannat is often blended with Merlot or Pinot Noir to soften it, or with Marselan. Some producers even co-ferment a little white Viognier, adding aroma and helping colour.

steps.explanation: Crushing seeds releases harsh tannin, the opposite of what you want.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Micro-oxygenation was invented in Madiran in 1991 for Tannat
Ripe picking, gentle extraction and oak soften it
Blending with Cabernet Franc or Merlot adds softness
